column1: Housing census – Conventional dwellings – Time series from 2011 on
column2: The Housing census included in the Register-based census and in the Register-based labour market statistics is a complete survey of the buildings and dwellings and their attributes for the reference date 31 October. The Register-based census and the Register-based labour market statistics are conducted by using information from administrative registers. The main data source for the Housing census is the Buildings- and dwellings register of Statistics Austria. The characteristics and definitions are based on the EU regulation on population and housing censuses and the Austrian Register-based census act (BGBl. I. Nr. 33/2006). For a detailed description of the methods used and for further information see: https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/housing/stock-of-buildings https://www.statistik.at/en/statistics/population-and-society/housing/stock-of-dwellings https://www.statistik.at/fileadmin/shared/QM/Standarddokumentationen/B_1/std_b_abgestimmte_erwerbsstatistik.pdf (German only) This database contains the results for all conventional dwellings. Conventional dwellings are structurally separate premises which are designed for permanent human habitation at a fixed location, with direct access from the street or from a public staircase. They consist of one room or suite of rooms as well as side rooms. The existence of a kitchen or kitchenette is not crucial. Rooms in hotels, student residencies and similar buildings are not counted as conventional dwellings. .) Territorial structure of 2022. .) Updating: annually last update: [2024-06-17] .) For analyses based on very small cell values, no reliable assertions can be made.

column1: Age of the household reference person [partly ABO]
column2: Age in completed years at the respective reference date. Calculated from the date of birth. Household reference person: - oldest person of the family nucleus in one-family households, - oldest person of the middle generation in households with two or more family nuclei, - oldest person in households without family nucleus.

column1: Sex of the household reference person
column2: In order to guarantee protection of data privacy, persons with a third sex category are not separately reported. They are imputed either as "male" or "female". Household reference person: - oldest person of the family nucleus in one-family households, - oldest person of the middle generation in households with two or more family nuclei, - oldest person in households without family nucleus.
